patients with multiple sclerosis have polymorphic psychological disorders, including personality and cognitive disorders, neuropsychiatric symptoms and "internal picture of illness" that is not adequate to the real state of disease.

psychological disorders in multiple sclerosis and their influence on the treatment and rehabilitation.
the study of psychological disorders and their influence on the course of multiple sclerosis.
the role of psychological factors in the development of multiple sclerosis.

the psychological disorders of patients with multiple slerosis are the result of both the cerebral and psychological factors and that the treatment of psychological disorders should be carried out in close cooperation with neurologist and psychologist.
the psychological disorders in multiple sclerosis patients are not a result of psychological factors alone but are the result of the interaction between psychological and cerebral factors.
the patients with multiple sclerosis are characterized by a complex of psychological disorders, including cognitive and personality disorders, and neuropsychological symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multiple sclerosis is a disease of the brain and the nervous system, and it is a psychological disease, too.
the psychological disorders are not a separate nosological entity in patients with multiple scleroses.
multiple sclerosis is a disease of the central nervous system, which is accompanied by a complex of psychological disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
psychological factors are of great importance for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
the psychological disorders are not a consequence of the disease but are its integral part.
the psychological disorders of patients with multiple scleroses are determined not only by psychological factors, but also by the functional state of the central nervous system.
